Problem

Prove that there exist two functions , such that is strictly decreasing and is strictly increasing.

Source

Romanian Master of Mathematics Competition 2011 Problems

Key Idea
  1. Partition into two alternating families of half-open intervals.
  2. Construct two piecewise affine functions that preserve or exchange these families in a carefully designed manner.
  3. Intra-interval ordering: Choose the slopes of the functions to ensure the desired monotonicity of their compositions within each interval.
    Design the coefficients of the affine functions carefully so that the images of different intervals lie within specific intervals.
  4. Inter-interval ordering: Choose suitable index functions to arrange the images of consecutive intervals in the correct order.

Inspiration: necessity

The previous section lacks sufficient contexts about how we come up with the construction of and , which is rather complicated.
Thus, some inspiration shared in the following sections, not parts of the proof, could be helpful for one attempting to catch my idea.

The original problem requires a proof of the existence of two functions with strictly decreasing and strictly increasing (or such and in brief).
My strategy is finding a constructive proof, as I believe that finding a nonconstructive one for this problem would not be easier, and also that there would be infinitely many pair of such and , including one whose forms may be expressible within my ability.
In order to imagine probable forms of such and , analyzing necessary conditions for such and might be helpful.

What We Learned

This problem illustrates how a seemingly paradoxical requirement involving function compositions can be approached through a carefully designed partition of the domain.

By separating intra-interval monotonicity from inter-interval ordering, we can transform a difficult functional construction into a system of inequalities involving integer-valued index functions.

It also demonstrates the usefulness of working backward from the desired properties of a construction: instead of guessing the functions directly, we first determine how their compositions should act on a suitable partition of the real line.
